anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
## Pick boundary

At every work pick, I save the run record first, including course, accounting and the pick's payload snapshot. Work starts only after that save. Nothing is re-initialized: the existing tracker gets each later stage (`menu`, then the loop's stages) only when that stage starts. The commit being assessed is aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa unless a step below says otherwise.

| Pick | course | work_started | Accounting / other record writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: 2 deliver | deliver | true | Caps stay 10/10; rounds and syncs stay 0/0; a no-progress checkpoint is saved after the dispatch. |
| B: 3 assess | assess | true (one review post) | Usage unchanged; the posted review becomes the new GitHub baseline at aaaa…. |
| C: 2 deliver | deliver | true | Rounds go to 1/10 after the counted commit; syncs stay 0/10; pushed_head becomes bbbb…. |
| D: 5 back | null | false | reject_withdrawn true; no payload is applied and the record is otherwise unchanged. |
| deliver with nits | deliver-nits | true | Accounting initialized if missing. |
| fix nits, course null | null (unchanged) | true | One-shot `repair.wave.action: fix-nits` with selected_ids and payload snapshots; missing accounting initialized from defaults. |
| approve workflow run | unchanged | true | Course stays as set; the watch runs under that existing course. |
| approve | unchanged | true | approved_head is written only after gh succeeds. |
| merge | unchanged | true | Nothing is written until the merge compare-and-swap passes. |
| assess, zero blockers | assess | false | Nothing is posted and the GitHub baseline is unchanged. |
| show evidence | unchanged | false | Prints the full record and re-renders the same menu. |
| check test flaky | unchanged | false | Records a human disposition only; no command runs and no course is set. |
| overrule 1 | unchanged | false | Treated as a change request; no course is set and nothing runs. |
| invalid input | unchanged | false | One clarifying question naming the valid range; nothing runs. |
| reject-menu step | unchanged | false | menus.md defines no handler for posting the note, closing the PR or disposing P1, so nothing is executed. |

## A - deliver, fixture missing

These steps run in order:

1. Run the Exit check, which passes.
2. Run the merge-tree check, which is clean, so no sync runs.
3. Write the finding artifacts: the derived spec and the ledger, each with one row for P1.
4. Dispatch `loop-implementer` with `cwd /work/widgets-pr-88` and an output file of its own in `${TMPDIR}`. The task carries:
   - the shared worker context;
   - the scope baseline;
   - the HEAD check against aaaa…;
   - the scoped test commands;
   - the pi tail, including the `needs <what>` rule;
   - the row-dispatch fields.

The helper returns a failed decision whose second slot reads `needs source fixture`, with no commit. No round is charged. The Exit check then matches its "helper needs" row and the no-progress checkpoint is saved.

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR moves the widget indexing job onto the existing change feed. No spec governs it, so it is judged against the PR's own description.

One problem blocks merging. The indexing job keeps its own copy of the catalog, but the architecture doc on main says indexing must read the shared change feed (docs/architecture.md:12). The repair attempt stopped because it needs a source fixture that is not in the repository, so retrying without one would fail the same way.

I recommend stop, because no other choice can make progress until that fixture exists.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - retry the repair once the source fixture is available. This adds ten repair attempts and ten sync attempts to this run's allowance.
3. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review comment and make no repairs.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

## B - assess

These steps run in order:

1. Run the output done-check on the review body.
2. Run the compare-and-swap, which matches.
3. Post the review:

   `gh api --method POST repos/example/widgets/pulls/88/reviews -f commit_id=aaaa… -f event=COMMENT -f body=<composed body>`

   The event is COMMENT because this is your own PR. The response's commit_id equals aaaa…, which confirms the baseline.

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/assess-terminal recommended=1

This PR moves the widget indexing job onto the existing change feed. No spec governs it, so it is judged against the PR's own description.

One problem still blocks merging. The indexing job keeps a separate catalog copy, which contradicts the architecture doc (docs/architecture.md:12). That problem is now posted on the PR as a review comment.

I recommend stop, because nothing has changed since the review was posted.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR with the posted review. [recommended]
2. deliver - switch to repairing the problem, then watch the checks until merge is offered.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

## C - deliver, repaired and pushed

The run reaches the final menu in these steps:

1. **Repair.** The same `loop-implementer` dispatch as in A returns one commit that implements the change feed. That commit counts as one round.
2. **Review before the push.** A fresh `wave-reviewer` reviews `aaaa…..HEAD`, with `cwd` the worktree. Its task has two parts:
   - the re-review contract, with P1 as the previous report;
   - the fix delta `git diff aaaa… HEAD`.

   The reviewer reports `P1: resolved` and no new findings.
3. **Push.** One push runs:

   `git -C /work/widgets-pr-88 push --no-follow-tags <head_url> HEAD:refs/heads/<head_ref>`

   It moves the head to bbbb….
4. **After the push.** No claim recheck and no whole-wave review run. The run does the following:
   - runs the pre-menu refresh and finds CI green on bbbb…;
   - refetches comments and finds no delta;
   - renders the report from the reviewer's closure lines.

   Merge preconditions all hold, including the plan-free head check and squash being allowed. The commit being assessed is now bbbb….

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/final recommended=1

This PR moves the widget indexing job onto the existing change feed. No spec governs it, so it is judged against the PR's own description.

Nothing blocks merging. The separate catalog copy is gone, and the job now reads the shared change feed as the architecture doc requires. Required checks passed in CI on the pushed commit.

I recommend merge, because every merge requirement holds.

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge this PR into main. [recommended]
2. stop - leave the PR open and keep the checkout as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

## D - back to the first menu

The run returns to the first menu in these steps:

1. Run the pre-menu refresh. The head is unchanged at aaaa…, P1 is still open, and nothing runs.
2. Render the menu from menus.md. menus.md has no reject row, so the menu is built from its own action rows rather than the earlier reject mapping.

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR moves the widget indexing job onto the existing change feed. No spec governs it, so it is judged against the PR's own description.

One problem blocks merging. The indexing job keeps its own catalog copy, contrary to the architecture doc (docs/architecture.md:12). The drafted fix removes that copy and reads the change feed instead, which keeps the PR's indexing promise.

I recommend deliver, because a repair is drafted and needs no decision from you.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair the problem, rebase on main if needed, watch the checks, and repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review comment and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
These are independent continuations of the existing run, not new invocations: no tracker initialization, provisioning, or verification is repeated. I save each valid selection and its accounting changes before entering its handler; an unchanged missing prerequisite is checked before any further repair or watch.

`work_started` is synthetic bookkeeping here, not additional authority. The supplied protocol does not define `reject`, `reject_withdrawn`, or `overrule` handlers, so those names grant no permission to post, close, or dismiss a blocker.

| Checkpoint or boundary probe | Saved record effects |
|---|---|
| A: deliver | Set `course=deliver`, `work_started=true`; retain initial usage and caps. Save the returned `needs source fixture` result and unchanged prerequisite before rendering the obstacle. No source-changing commit means no repair round is charged. |
| B: assess | Set `course=assess`, `work_started=true`. Retain the successful head-pinned COMMENT review and its matching commit as the posted baseline. Keep the blocker open. |
| C: deliver | Set `course=deliver`, `work_started=true`. Charge one source-changing repair round, with no sync charged. Retain the reviewer’s resolved closure, successful push, and exact-head evidence for `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. |
| D: back | Execute no post, close, or cleanup step. Keep `course=null` and `work_started=false`; refresh the unchanged PR and return to the initial action menu. No supplied rule authorizes changing `reject_withdrawn`. |
| deliver with nits | Before its handler: `work_started=true`, `course=deliver-nits`. |
| fix nits, initially no course | Before its handler: `work_started=true`, `course=null`; persist the one-shot selected findings and payloads, not a standing delivery course. |
| approve workflow run | Before its handler: `work_started=true`; leave the existing course unchanged. |
| approve | Before its handler: `work_started=true`; leave the existing course unchanged. Do not set `approved_head` before success. |
| merge | Before its handler: `work_started=true`; leave the existing course unchanged. A selection does not establish that merging succeeded. |
| assess with zero blockers | Before its handler: `work_started=true`, `course=assess`. Its handler posts nothing. |
| show evidence | Inspection only; neither field changes. |
| check test flaky | A direct check-disposition command, not course selection; neither field changes. It can classify only the named failing check, not the architecture blocker. No command runs in this probe. |
| overrule 1 | Not a recognized disposition command; treat it as a change request. Neither field changes and nothing is overridden. |
| Invalid input | Execute nothing; neither field changes. Clarify an invalid numeric selection against the retained mapping. |
| Reject-menu step | Its name alone establishes no supported handler or authority. Neither field changes and no command runs in this probe. |

### A — Missing fixture

The saved helper result is evaluated before any additional repair or CI watch. The missing source fixture remains the obstacle; increasing the attempt limits would not supply it.

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

One problem blocks merging: the indexing job maintains a second catalog contrary to docs/architecture.md:12; for example, it stores its own catalog instead of consuming the existing change feed. Repair cannot continue without the source fixture, and no source change, review, push, or CI watch followed the failed repair dispatch.

I recommend stop because the missing source fixture has not changed.

Pick one:
1. stop - end this run without posting a review or changing the PR. [recommended]
2. deliver - continue after the source fixture becomes available, adding ten repair attempts and ten sync attempts; the unchanged missing fixture still prevents work.
3. assess - post the open problem as a review and make no repairs.

### B — Assessment posted

The successful COMMENT review is retained as the assessed-head baseline. Posting it does not resolve the architecture defect.

1. stop - end the assessment and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]
2. deliver - switch to repairing the blocker, rebase on main if needed, watch CI, and continue until merge is offered.

### C — Repair ready to merge

Before the push, review covers the repair delta from the previously pushed commit through the local repair commit and checks closure of the catalog-copy finding. After the push, there is no whole-diff review or repeated claim check: the exact pushed commit uses the pre-push closure, refreshed CI evidence, and comment reconciliation; there is no comment delta requiring source review.

Verification and the brief’s evidence assessment now bind to `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`, not the original commit.

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/final recommended=1

This PR adds indexing by consuming the existing change feed instead of keeping a separate catalog copy. You are its author, and the repaired implementation covers the indexing promise while following the documented architecture.

Nothing blocks merging. The reviewer confirmed that the separate-copy problem is resolved, CI passed for the pushed commit, and comment reconciliation found no changes requiring review; you cannot approve your own PR.

I recommend merge because the repair is pushed and every merge prerequisite passes.

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge the reviewed change. [recommended]
2. stop - leave the ready PR open without merging.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

### D — Back without executing a step

The retained mapping resolves row 5 to back. No note is posted, the PR is not closed, and no cleanup runs; the refreshed unchanged PR returns to the initial action menu, which has no reject row in the supplied menus.md.

I recommend deliver because the change-feed repair preserves the PR’s indexing promise and requires no author decision.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair the blocker, rebase on main if needed, watch CI, and repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review and make no repairs.
3. stop - end this run without posting or changing the PR.
